subject: Archaeology
title: The Greenland Norse: Vikings Who Vanished
description: A 60-second lesson on The Greenland Norse: Vikings Who Vanished.

hook.text: Vikings settled Greenland in 985 CE and thrived for 500 years. By the 1400s, they were gone. No one knows exactly why.

buildup.text: The Norse established farms, churches, and trade routes. At their peak, about 5,000 people lived in two settlements.

discovery.text: Excavations show they raised cattle and sheep but refused to eat fish or learn Inuit hunting methods — a fatal cultural.

twist.text: The Little Ice Age cooled Greenland severely. Sea ice blocked trade ships.

climax.text: The last known record is a 1408 wedding. After that, silence. No graves of the final settlers have ever been found.

punchline.text: They farmed in a place meant for hunting. The ice returned and the ships.

quiz.question: What cultural failure contributed to the Greenland Norse collapse?
options: They converted to a religion that forbade them from eating land animals
They refused to eat fish or learn Inuit hunting methods despite worsening conditions
They waged constant war against neighboring Inuit settlements
